segments.narration: A wave in Alaska tore out trees 524 metres up. That is higher than any building standing on Earth today.
On the ninth of July, 1958, the Fairweather Fault slipped, somewhere between magnitude seven point eight and eight point three.
It shook loose the head of a narrow inlet. Thirty million cubic metres of rock dropped into deep water at once.
In a fjord that narrow the water cannot spread. It climbed the opposite slope and sheared off mature forest at a clean line.
Fishing boats were anchored inside. One was carried over the treetops; both aboard lived to describe it. On another boat, two died.
